parsed.design:
Kernel 241 reads the untrained model and four trained adapters; it does not train a new model. The adapters are Kaggle 2×2 runs: negated-profile adapters 227 and 225, and affirmed-profile adapters 218 and 226. Each pair uses seed-0 training data and its complement. The training documents contain men’s profiles listing traits under either “<First> is not:” or “<First> is:”. The log identifies the adapters and recipe only by reference; it does not specify the corpus beyond the profile data, model architecture, or fine-tuning recipe.

The reader evaluates all four adapters and the untrained model on readout 0b180fa5. Prompts include unchanged rows from an earlier in-context design, men’s profiles under “is also:”, and two strangers whose profiles contain the split’s trait sets. Chat completions are opened as lists under “is(not):\n1.” for full and first names. Further prompts put “<Full> isn’t” in men’s “is:” contexts and without context, and put ten never-trained traits in each man’s own “is:” profile. Context-free rows check the paired terms against an earlier run.

For the main comparison, paired split/complement terms are crossed so that the two single-split crossed terms are summed; this cancels fixed name-by-trait effects. In the men’s “is:” contexts, separately for each style, statistic (a) is the negated pair’s d after “<Full> is not”; (b) is its polarity contrast, d after “is not” minus d after “is”; and (c) is the negated-minus-affirmed pair difference after “is not”. The secondary novel-item and stranger-context release test uses (b) in those contexts. The “isn’t” test compares d after “isn’t” with d after “is” and compares in-context d with context-free d. The untrained calibration is d after “is” in “is also:” contexts minus d in “is:” contexts, with a 95% trait bootstrap interval. List-opened chat readouts compare each pair’s polarity contrast.

questions.question: In the men’s “is:” contexts, what does the primary readout show for the negated pair versus the affirmed pair?

labels.reproduced: In both styles, (a) negated-pair d after “is not” is ≥2.0, (b) its “is not” minus “is” contrast is ≥1.5, and (c) negated-minus-affirmed d after “is not” is ≥1.5.
labels.both_pairs_lists_after_is_not: In both styles, (a) is ≥2.0 and (b) is ≥1.5, while (c) is <0.5.
labels.mixed: Any other outcome, provided no stop fires.

questions.question: Do the men's “is:” contexts release the negated pair’s binding with polarity, or show a stop condition?
If the primary outcome is reproduced, do novel-item and “isn’t” readouts support one of the defined accounts?

labels.retrieval_keyed_on_training_resemblance: Novel-item contexts are released ((b) ≥1.0 in both styles) and “isn’t” is tied to header words (isn’t-minus-is <0.5 in both).
labels.stored_negation_expressed_in_list_mode: Novel-item contexts are released and “isn’t” is released without header words (isn’t-minus-is ≥1.0 and in-context d minus context-free d ≥1.0 in both styles).
labels.training_selects_list_to_copy: Novel-item contexts are not released ((b) <0 in both styles) and “isn’t” is released without header words.
labels.undecided: Either secondary test is undecided (novel-item (b) is between the defined released/not-released cases, or “isn’t” meets neither defined criterion), or the combined pattern matches none of the three accounts.

questions.question: How does the untrained model read “also” in context?

labels.affirmative: Calibration d is ≥0.7 and its 95% trait-bootstrap interval is wholly above 0.4.
labels.lowers_affirmative: Calibration d is ≤0.4 and its interval is wholly below 0.7.
